newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Fed's Angell says no rate rise while dlr strong.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Fed's Angell says no rate rise while dlr strong.

text.p: Former Federal Reserve Governor Wayne Angell said Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan would resist raising official interest rates with the dollar at it's current relatively high level.
"I just don't think he wants to (raise rates) with the dollar already being so strong," Angell said in an interview on CNBC on Wednesday.
"I think he is very happy with the situation and I think he will wait awhile before he would ever decide to raise rates."
Angell was complimentary of Greenspan's track record when discussing the chairman's recent "irrational exuberance" remark concerning the equity markets.

"I think the Fed chairman has done such a wonderful job outweighing the Federal Reserve in regard to sound monetary policy that it just isn't worthwhile for him to tarnish his record by forecasting something he's not very good at forecasting," Angell said.
Angell stressed that Fed policymakers should not factor the sharp rise of U.S. stock markets into their decision making.
"I don't believe that rising equity prices...is in and of itself a sign that the Federal Reserve has provided too much liqudity," he said.
"I think monetary policy is okay. And I think monetary policy makers should not take the stock market into consideration as they deliberate."
